title: Mitochondria Lipid Encapsulation for Transfer Therapy Protocol
author: Hamanaka, Back, et al.

steps.title: Assemble dual‑tube system
steps.instruction: Sanitize a sharp blade with 70 % EtOH, cut the bottom of a 0.6 mL microtube 3 cm from the lid to create a ~4 mm diameter hole, autoclave both the 0.6 mL tube and a 1.5 mL tube, insert the cut tube (inner) into the 1.5 mL tube (outer), add 500 µL PBS to the inner tube so it flows through the hole into the outer tube, and keep the assembled system until use, ensuring the PBS level in the inner tube remains higher than in the outer tube if different tube types are used.

steps.title: Isolate mitochondria from placenta
steps.instruction: Place a frozen rat placenta on a 35 mm dish, add 500 µL mitobuffer, chop the tissue into small pieces, transfer the pieces to a grinder with mitobuffer, rinse the dish with another 500 µL mitobuffer and add to the grinder (total 1 mL in grinder), grind on ice ~30–40 strokes, transfer homogenate to a 15 mL tube, rinse the grinder with 500 µL mitobuffer and add to the tube (total 1.5 mL), centrifuge sequentially: 700 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; collect supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube, then 2,000 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; collect supernatant, then 4,000 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; collect supernatant, finally 8,000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min, discard supernatant, suspend the pellet in 200 µL mitobuffer (or 50–100 µL if pellet is small), and determine mitochondrial protein concentration using a protein assay (e.g., Bradford or BCA) with BSA standards on a 96‑well plate measured at 595 nm.

steps.title: Prepare mitochondria suspension
steps.instruction: Measure mitochondrial protein concentration, aliquot 50–100 µg mitochondria into a 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge at 8,000 g for 10 min, discard the supernatant completely, then resuspend the pellet in exactly 10 µL suspension buffer (ratio 10 µg mitochondria per 1 µL buffer, total buffer ≤10 µL).

steps.title: Make lipid mixture in oil
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube add 300 µL mineral oil, then add 3 µL of 100 mM DOPE and 1 µL of 300 mM DOTAP, vortex to mix well, and centrifuge at 1,000 g for 1 min to eliminate air bubbles, yielding the lipid nanoparticle solution.

steps.title: Create mitochondria‑lipid emulsion
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of the lipid nanoparticle solution (from the previous step) into a new 1.5 mL tube, add 10 µL of the mitochondria suspension (from step 3), and pipette gently about 10 times to form a water‑in‑oil (W/O) emulsion.

steps.title: Optional: Western blot verification
steps.instruction: Dissolve the lipid‑coated mitochondria (MitoCoat) and a non‑coated control in appropriate volumes of sample buffer, heat at 85 °C for 10 min (skip heating when probing OXPHOS), load 15–20 µL per well and run SDS‑PAGE at 100 V for 60 min (PowerEase 300 W), prepare 5 % skim milk in TBST as blocking buffer, transfer proteins to a PVDF membrane using iBlot 2 for 7 min (preset P0), block the membrane in 5 % skim milk/TBST at room temperature for 1 h on a shaker, dilute primary antibodies in 1 % skim milk/TBST (OXPHOS 1:500, Tomm 40 1:1,000, Tom 20 1:1,000, β‑Actin 1:10,000) and incubate at 4 °C for ~15 h, wash membrane with TBST at room temperature for 10 min, five times, dilute secondary antibodies in 1 % skim milk/TBST (anti‑rabbit HRP 1:1,000, anti‑mouse HRP 1:1,000), add secondary and incubate at room temperature for 1 h, wash again with TBST (10 min, five times), prepare SuperSignal™ West Pico PLUS Luminol/Enhancer, treat membrane on plastic wrap for 1 min in the dark, image on a G:Box with exposure times of 30 s, 1 min, 3 min, 5 min, 8 min, 10 min, 15 min, and 20 min, and save JPEG files for analysis. Note: Use PVDF membrane for OXPHOS detection, do not heat samples when probing OXPHOS, and adjust enhancer or exposure as needed.

description: Our protocol describes a method for modifying mitochondria to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of mitochondrial transplantation. Mitochondrial transplantation is recognized as a promising strategy to restore ATP production in metabolically compromised cells. Our lab has studied the role of intercellular mitochondrial transfer and mitochondria transplantation in vivo and in vitro, where we observed mitochondrial uptake and overall efficacy.2,3,4,5 Although various approaches to mitochondrial modification to amplify the efficacy have been developed, our protocol offers a convenient, straightforward, and efficient method to boost ATP levels in both cellular and animal models. This strategy holds significant potential for translating basic research findings into clinical applications. This section provides a detailed protocol for mitochondria modification using artificial lipids composed of DOPE and DOTAP. This method enables researchers to conveniently encapsulate mitochondria with artificial or biological lipid components as needed —referred to as MitoCoat—for use in both cell-based and animal studies. The MitoCoat strategy offers a straightforward approach for mitochondrial surface modification, facilitating broader application in experimental and therapeutic research.
